clauses.reason: The order approves the code and makes the approval subject to a condition: "Now, Therefore, I, Franklin D. Roosevelt, President of the United States, pursuant to the authority vested in me by title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, approved June 16, 1933, and otherwise, do adopt and approve the report, recommendations, and findings of the Administrator, and do order that the said code of fair competition be and is hereby approved, subject to the following condition:" An approved code had legal effect through NIRA section 3 (standard of fair competition under 3(b), injunction under 3(c), misdemeanor under 3(f)). Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 (49 Stat. 375), approved June 14, 1935, repealed "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes". The resolution states no effective date other than its approval. That repeal removed the prospective operative effect of this command, so its first end is June 14, 1935. June 16, 1935 is not the end, and Schechter (May 27, 1935, section 3 delegation held unconstitutional) is a validity characterization, not an end date.

The condition provides that the application of section 5, article III, as to the payment of time and one-third for hours over forty a week, "shall be stayed until January 1, 1934," The stay therefore ends on its own terms on January 1, 1934, a date before June 14, 1935, which makes that date the first end of this stay. Under the owner's 2026-10-21 until-date ruling the end is recorded as the stated date, inclusive (the stay runs through the end of January 1, 1934). The exclusive reading, that the stay ends when January 1, 1934 begins, is stated as the alternative and is the more natural reading of the next clause, which makes the provisions effective "at which time"; both readings give the same stated date. The repeal of June 14, 1935 is a later event for this clause and not its end.

The order provides: "at which time such provisions shall become effective and have the same force and effect as any other provision of the code." Under the stay's own terms the provisions became part of the code on January 1, 1934 and from then had the force of any other code provision. inventory_overrides.reason: Operative approval of the code, ending at the colon that introduces the condition.
The stay clause of the condition, with its own stated end date, separated from the approval and from the activation that follows it.
The activation clause: after the stay the stayed provisions take effect as ordinary code provisions, a separate command from the stay itself and one that depends on the code.

research_rationale:
Identity: the census register lists EO 6393 dated 1933-11-04 (Franklin D. Roosevelt); the WPA 1944 list entry for 1933 Nov 4, p.547, records the code for the Toy and Playthings Industry as approved, and the held text's date and subject agree. APP page check passed: the mirror page record with the held text's sha256 (common-crawl capture) has a heading naming this order's number, the same date and subject, and a text_sha256 equal to the held text's. The held text was read in full. Own terms: the approval has none; the stay carries an own-terms end ("until January 1, 1934"), recorded as the first end of the stay clause only, while the approval and the activation clause end by the repeal. Repeal route per the reviewed shared analysis: an approval under section 3 depended on the code approval and enforcement provisions that section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 repealed on June 14, 1935; Schechter (May 27, 1935) is recorded only as a validity characterization.

savings.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the approved code before June 14, 1935 are accrued; the NIRA section 5 antitrust exemption for action complying with the code during the period is an accrued effect for past action only. The proviso in section 2 of the resolution limits the section 5 exemption to agreements and action thereunder that put section 7(a) requirements into effect or prohibit practices already unlawful, names agreements rather than codes and states no time limit, and the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the exemption for past action. Nothing held continues the approval after June 14, 1935.
